blindSummary:
Risk here is limited, with strong legal protections and institutional responses, but a more acute violence context than neighbouring countries. Legal gender recognition by self-declaration since 2016; hate speech against trans people is criminalised (2020); anti-discrimination law covers gender identity; and the police operate a dedicated hate-crime unit, with the domestic security service providing annual threat assessments around Pride events.

The offsetting factors: a supporter of a designated terrorist organisation shot and killed two people at the capital's Pride event in 2022 and was sentenced to 30 years; police-reported hate crimes against queer and trans people rose sharply in 2023 (up 18% overall, with trans-specific reports nearly doubling); an anti-gender movement is growing; and underreporting barriers are documented. The security service reports a significant decline in threats for 2025 Pride events, but hate-speech and intimidation risks persist.

Bathrooms are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation, and the shared visa-free border area poses no trans-specific friction.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory beyond one foreign government's updated advisory that mentions this country; general urban crime is very low.
blindSourceSummaries: Official page on legal gender change: under the gender-recognition act, individuals determine their legal gender based on their own perception of gender identity (self-declaration via the tax administration); from age 16 alone, ages 6-16 with parents; under-6s only for documented congenital DSD; a 2017 regulation covers citizens resident abroad.

Regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: reported hate crimes rose 18% in 2023, with the largest increases in crimes motivated by sexual orientation, gender identity/expression and religious hatred; the perpetrator of a 2022 mass shooting at the capital's Pride event was sentenced to 30 years (the strictest penalty); a drag event sparked online threats; a knife attack on two people investigated as a hate crime.
NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying newswire report (2020) covers this country outlawing hate speech against trans people (an amendment to the criminal code).

Public broadcaster (May 2024): big increase in reported hate crime against queer and trans people - record numbers reporting, but the clearance rate fell from 52% to 45% in 2023 and many cases are dropped; many victims have little trust in police; a special hate-crime unit encourages reporting.

University research centre on extremism and political violence (Sept 2024): contextualising transphobia in this country - hostility manifests among political extremists and religious fundamentalists; a neo-fascist movement openly advocates destroying LGBTQ rights; research interviews show far-right views of gender diversity as 'degeneracy' and 'paedophilia-normalising'.

Same research centre (June 2025): why anti-LGBTQI hate crimes are not reported to the police - a hate-crime reporting study of 3,000+ survey responses found only 8% of victims reported; mistrust in police, procedural obstacles and fear of personal costs; those who did report described dismissive or condescending treatment.

Regional security-organisation page on this country's national hate-crime frameworks: hate crimes defined as criminal offences motivated by hatred due to ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation etc.

Regional online outlet (April 2025): the country's domestic security service reports a 'significant decline' in threats against LGBTQ+ events and individuals over the past year, but warns hate speech and intimidation risks remain, especially during Pride; most threat-makers aim to spread fear rather than act.

Resettlement-information site (updated Nov 2020): national LGBT resources - residents generally hold liberal attitudes; this was among the first countries with anti-discrimination laws; gay and lesbian people have equal rights in religious wedding ceremonies, adoption and assisted pregnancy; directory of national support organisations (youth, trans and Pride groups).
blindLocalsOnly: The self-declaration gender-recognition regime (2016) and the criminalised hate-speech provision (2020) are resident-facing.
